paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend. When the LORD says something is coming, it comes, no matter how impossible it looks from where you're standing. The city was starving, the king had given up on waiting, and the officer asked if it could really happen. Then Elisha's word landed exactly as spoken, and the flour sold for a shekel "according to the word of the LORD" (2 Kings 7:16).

Now look at HOW the LORD did it. He used four men with leprosy, sitting at the gate with nothing left to lose. A whole army ran off, and those four were the first to find out. I think that's the LORD telling us He doesn't need the strong, the important or the ones who have it figured out to do His work. He can use anybody, and that includes you, friend.

Then the four men did the part I can't stop thinking about. They stopped, looked at what they were doing, and said, "We are not doing what is right. Today is a day of good news" (2 Kings 7:9). Good news is not for hiding in a tent, and it's too good to keep to yourself. So the next time the Word of God fills you up, go tell somebody, because there's a whole city out there still hungry, and you know where the flour is!
